Careful — the substrate doesn't show that yet, and what it does show currently leans the other way.

The largest measured effect in this whole project is runtime context, not weights: ~40 points of holdout fabrication moved on whether the receipts were in the prompt, identical across both tuned models, while the corpus rebuild moved 0–1. Your own note from that night: *"a model cannot invent what it can copy — so the lever is the prompt at runtime, not the training data."*

And the 2×2 that would actually test your claim has a missing cell — **untuned base + the v3.1 system prompt was never run.** Without it, tuned-with-prompt 21/24 can't be separated from "the prompt does the work."

`SYSTEM-v31.txt` is the 3999-char prompt from your screenshot, and `qwen3.6:27b` is still resident from the control run — same model, no swap, nothing else generating. Running the missing cell.

**Missing cell: untuned base + SYSTEM-v31 = 15/24, 1 drift.** That changes the reading, and it goes your way on this axis.

Result, and where I was wrong:

| weights | bare | + SYSTEM-v31 (3999 chars) |
|---|---|---|
| untuned qwen3.6:27b | 12/24 | **15/24**, 1 drift |
| arch-gov-27b-v31 | 15/24 | **21/24**, 0 drift |

I framed the fabrication result as if it settled the whole question. It doesn't. Training is worth **+3 bare and +6 with the prompt present** — the two levers compound rather than substitute, which is the opposite shape from the holdout finding.

The item that actually carries your argument isn't the totals — it's **V2**. The untuned base emits APPROVE/REVISE/REJECT at the scanner seat in *both* conditions: bare, and with all 3999 characters of directives sitting in context. The prompt does not fix it. v3.1 holds it in both. That's a reflex — a boundary that has to hold without being re-read — and context at that length cannot buy it.

On your second point: that's already your own recorded diagnosis, not a hypothesis. The scorecard's lesson from v3.1 is *structural beats additive* — the fabrication fix took because the defective slot was deleted from every target; the seat fix didn't because 21 rows were added against 187 conductor rows and lost. v3.2 then repaired the data correctly and got a worse model on all three axes. "The tuning is failing because the governance isn't being trained right" is the finding on disk.
